sections.heading: C — Signals, Signs, and Markers
sections.markdown:
## C — Signals, Signs, and Markers

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Drivers obey every signal unless an officer directs otherwise, and officer orders stand even against ordinary law, with steady red demanding a stop ahead of the crosswalk or intersection before any lawful right turn or any left turn joining one one-way street from another, always yielding to pedestrians and legal intersection users [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Flashing red means stop fully then go when safe while cross traffic may roll on, steady yellow orders a safe stop or a cautious clearing, flashing yellow orders slower caution, flashing yellow left arrows permit left turns against yielding to oncoming cars, steady green permits straight or turning travel with intersection watchfulness, green arrows beside red permit careful arrow-direction travel after yielding, and plain green lefts yield to all oncoming traffic [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Traffic signs warn of hidden hazards ahead, guide travelers along routes, publish local rules and habits, and regulate speed and movement [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A02
Sign colors read red for stop, yield, or posted orders, green for allowed moves and direction, blue for motorist services, yellow for warning, black and white for regulation, orange for construction and maintenance, reflective orange for varied signs, and brown for recreation and scenery [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A02
Sign shapes read octagon for stop only, horizontal rectangle for guides, triangle for yield only, pennant for no-passing advance notice, diamond for hazard warnings, vertical rectangle for regulations, pentagon for school zones and crossings, and circle for railroad advance notice, with warning signs demanding attention, obedience, and posted-speed slowing under violation risk [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A03
Early warnings flag signals ahead, underpass clearance against tall loads, median-divided highway starts, added lanes needing no merge, right-left reverse curves, joining side roads, rough surfaces, and crossing traffic, each answered with slowing, right-side keeping, and no passing where posted [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A03
Further warnings flag sharp arrowed turns, winding roads, divided-highway endings with returning two-way traffic, wet roads forbidding sudden moves, right-lane discipline against left-side oncoming cars, gradual arrowed curves, crossroads needing all-direction looks, and shrinking lane counts [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A04
More warnings mark T and Y junctions, merging lanes, heavy pedestrian zones, schools needing sudden-stop readiness, loose gravel forbidding sharp braking or turns, edge and pier obstruction markers, and short-alignment change markers [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A04
Still more warnings order T must-turns with yielding, dip slowdowns, soft-shoulder caution, narrow-bridge care, highway-junction looks and stop readiness, double sharp turns, winter ice-bridge gentleness, and night-alignment delineators [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A05
Continuing warnings allow either-side island passing, mark narrow-bridge rail ends, announce entering trucks, narrow pavements, pavement-to-earth transitions, edge drop-offs needing firm slow steering, grooved wet-weather grooves cautioning motorcyclists, and disabled or wheelchair crossings [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A05
Final warnings announce downgrades possibly needing low gear, metered ramps with flashing yellows and red-green meters, sudden humps, sharp curves, ending right lanes merging left, stop signs ahead, and animals [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A06
Regulatory signs bind like traffic laws, covering arrow-only turns, bus and carpool lanes weekday mornings six to nine, sight-limited yellow-line no-passing, double left-turn lanes with a mandatory left lane, disabled parking reserved to placarded vehicles, banned lefts, banned U-turns, and wrong-way one-way entry [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A06
More regulations order full stops with yielding and careful starts ahead of crosswalks and signs for every vehicle since slowing never suffices, plus advisory curve speeds, passing bans, slower-right discipline, safe ramp-exit speeds, posted day and night maximums, truck bans, and rightward island guidance [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A07
Further regulations bar opposite-direction one-way entry, command merge-and-yield manners, enforce flashing-yellow school speeds with child watchfulness, warn of red-light cameras, forbid double-white-line crossings, protect green-arrow lefts while urging caution, reserve shoulders for breakdown and emergency stops, close roads to detours, and merge all traffic single-file [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A07
Still more regulations mark divided-highway crossovers, ban wireless devices in school zones, run all-way stops by arrival order with right-side ties, push slower traffic off the passing-only far-left lane, confine center lanes to slowing or stopping left turns, green-light left turns, force right-lane right turns, and post advisory turn speeds [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A08
Guide signs orient strangers, rail advance signs warn within a few hundred feet to slow, ready a stop, and never race trains, crossbucks stand at every crossing showing track counts with slow-look-listen yielding, and emergency notification signs carry railroad numbers plus national inventory numbers pinpointing crossings [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A08
More guides point litter barrels a mile ahead and at rest areas, Texas and interstate markers name roads, overhead arrows assign route lanes, interstate mileposts pace emergencies every mile, exit-ahead lanes, short urban state highways, business branches, distance boards, and lane-use signals where red crosses close lanes, steady yellow crosses warn of lane-control changes, and green arrows open lanes [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A09
Gates demand stops at first flash before lowering and holds until raising with dark lights, rail stops land fifteen to fifty feet out on flaggers, red flashers with bells, or any train warnings, and markings show two-lane rural right-of-center discipline with broken-line passing only, free one-way lane choice with early turn positioning, center lanes entered solely to slow or stop for safe lefts, multi-lane double-yellow respect with slower-right habits, and center lanes never for passing or through travel [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A10
Solid yellow lines on the driver's side ban passing while broken lines allow safe passes and lane changes, white crosswalks define walker zones with stops ahead of them when signs, signals, or walkers require, white stop lines demand stops behind them, solid white edges and channelizers discourage crossing, left-edge interstate yellow forbids leftward travel, and double solid white forbids all crossing [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A11
Crash barrels cushion obstacles and crash-prone spots, hearing-impaired flags on bicycles and vehicles order slowing, orange work-zone devices spanning signs, barricades, panels, drums, cones, tubes, arrow boards, and flaggers demand slowdowns, lane changes, and worker alertness, work signs run mostly diamond with some rectangles, and traffic fines double in work zones where workers stand anywhere inside [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A12
Channelizing devices with night lights order slowing, safe lane changes, late-merger wariness, reduced speed to the zone-end sign, and checked returns, barricade stripes point the passing side by downward slope, arrow panels day and night assign lanes past closures, orange-clad flaggers with paddles and flags command in-lane stops without veering and motionless waits, and remote auto-flaggers plus pilot cars, warnings, and temp signals may assist [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A13
Defying warning signs, markings, or barricades is a misdemeanor fining one to two hundred dollars, doubled in staffed work zones and rising to Class B up to two thousand dollars and one hundred eighty days in jail at flooded roads, while slow-moving emblems belong solely on machines capped at twenty-five miles per hour including animal-drawn rigs, never elsewhere or on fixed objects, except in-zone construction machines and towed implements trailing emblemed movers [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0043]

items.why: Section Five is rule-and-recognition recall served by standard flashcards and quizzes; no separate practice mode is needed.

corpus_stability.reason: The Texas Driver Handbook is a periodically revised official edition, so Section Five signal rules change at most with new editions.

market_signal.origin_note: market signal is authored in part E
